chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: The JPJ Quartet
summary: Budd, Oliver Jackson and Bill Pemberton formed the quartet in 1969, played for Johns-Manville, then Yugoslavia and Montreal in 1971.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: '61. And I'm doing four original tunes now that the group that I'm with, which is the J.P.J. quartet --
Tell us a little about your group Budd there.
Okay. This is a group that was formed by Oliver Jackson, Bill Pimperton and myself after we left Earl in July of 1969. We formed this group and then ---
And what are you doing with that group, who have you been working for with that group?
Well, we worked for almost three years and were sponsored by the Johns Mansville Corporation and we were selected to play all of the high schools where they had plant locations which is in 24 cities.
In the United States. And we played some in Canada and we played one in Paris.
Well I remember you went to some far away country, what was that country you went to the with the JPJ group?
Oh, we were over in Europe, we played the Montreal Jazz Festival and --
No, what's the communist country over there?

We played there at their 12th annual jazz festival, and all of this was in 1971 and we were one of the hits there and we were one of the hits at the Montreal jazz festival at that year, which the film they've shown on us about three or four times here in the United States. And we also made an album from that, and I'm doing some full four original tunes now which we're supposed to perform, the JPJ quartet is going to perform in Washington, D. C. at the Kennedy Center with the youth symphony of Washington, D. C. 110 pieces.
